description: India's most important fruit tree; Andhra Pradesh and Telangana grow mainly Banganapalli, Totapuri and Suvarnarekha. New leaf flushes and the flowering period (December-February) are the stages most exposed to diseases and pests.
npk_split: For trees 10 years and older: apply half the N with all P and K and 50 kg FYM just after harvest (June-July) and the remaining N in September-October when the soil is moist.

Anthracnose.name: Anthracnose
Anthracnose.description: Fungal disease of tender leaves, flowers, twigs and fruits that is worst when rain or heavy dew falls during flushing and flowering. It causes blossom blight, fruit drop and black spots on ripening fruits.
symptoms: Irregular brown to black spots on young leaves, often starting at the margins and tip
Dead centres of spots fall out, leaving holes and tattered leaves
Flowers and panicle stalks turn black and dry
Young twigs dry back from the tip
Black sunken spots on fruits
Anthracnose.spread: Rain and dew splash spores from dead twigs, old panicles and infected leaves onto new flush, flowers and fruits.
Anthracnose.action: Prune and burn dead twigs and old panicles and spray a fungicide on the new flush and at panicle emergence.

treatment.name: Carbendazim 50 WP
treatment.notes: At panicle emergence and again at pea-size fruit stage.

treatment.name: Azoxystrobin 23 SC
treatment.notes: Alternative at flowering; also checks powdery mildew.

treatment.name: Copper oxychloride 50 WP
treatment.notes: After pruning and on new flush in the rainy season.

Bacterial canker.name: Bacterial Canker (Black Spot)
Bacterial canker.description: Bacterial disease of leaves, twigs and fruits that spreads in rainy, windy weather. Raised black cankers on fruits crack and ooze gum, causing fruit drop and loss of market value.
symptoms: Small water-soaked angular spots between the leaf veins
Spots become raised, black and rough with a yellow halo
Black cracked cankers on leaf stalks, twigs and fruits
Gum oozing from cracked fruit spots and early fruit drop
Bacterial canker.spread: Wind-driven rain, infected grafts and pruning tools carry the bacteria, which enter through leaf pores and wounds.
Bacterial canker.action: Prune out and burn infected twigs and spray a copper fungicide at 10-15 day intervals in wet weather.

treatment.name: Copper oxychloride 50 WP
treatment.notes: 2-3 sprays at 10-15 day intervals after the first spots are seen.

treatment.name: Disease-free grafts and windbreaks
treatment.notes: Take scion wood only from healthy trees; wind injury opens the way for infection.

Die back.name: Die Back
Die back.description: Fungal disease in which twigs and branches dry from the tip downward, most visible from October to December. Repeated attacks kill large limbs and can kill young or stressed trees.
symptoms: Twigs dry from the tip backward and the bark turns dark
Leaves on affected twigs turn brown, roll upward at the margins and fall
Bark cracks and oozes gum
Brown streaks inside the wood when the twig is split
Die back.spread: Spores spread by rain and wind enter through wounds, pruning cuts and graft unions, especially on trees stressed by drought or poor nutrition.
Die back.action: Prune dried twigs 5-10 cm below the dead part into healthy wood, burn them and paste the cut ends with copper fungicide.

treatment.name: Pruning of affected twigs below the dead wood
treatment.notes: Cut in dry weather and burn the prunings; take grafting wood only from healthy trees.

treatment.name: Copper oxychloride 50 WP paste or Bordeaux paste
treatment.notes: Apply the same day as pruning.

treatment.name: Copper oxychloride 50 WP
treatment.notes: Spray the tree after pruning and repeat after 15 days.

Gall midge.name: Leaf Gall Midge
Gall midge.description: Tiny midge flies lay eggs in tender leaves and the maggots feeding inside cause wart-like galls. Heavy galling makes leaves curl and drop early, reducing new growth.
symptoms: Many small raised wart-like galls on the leaf blade
Galls are green at first, later brown-black with a tiny exit hole
Heavily galled leaves crinkle, curl and fall early
Poor new flush on badly affected shoots
Gall midge.spread: Adult midges fly to new flushes to lay eggs, and several generations build up during flushing periods.
Gall midge.action: Clip off and burn heavily galled leaves and protect the next new flush with neem oil or a systemic insecticide.

treatment.name: Removal and burning of heavily galled shoots
treatment.notes: Do this before the next flush emerges.

treatment.name: Neem oil 1500 ppm
treatment.notes: At bud burst of the new flush and again 7-10 days later.

treatment.name: Imidacloprid 17.8 SL
treatment.notes: On new flush only if galling was heavy last season; do not spray on open flowers, to protect pollinators.

Leaf-cutting weevil.name: Leaf-Cutting Weevil
Leaf-cutting weevil.description: A small weevil that lays eggs in tender leaves and then cuts them off near the base. Nursery plants and young orchards lose their new flush and stop growing.
symptoms: Tender leaves cut straight across near the base, as if with scissors
Cut leaf pieces lying on the ground under the tree
Leaf stubs left on the new shoots
Small dark snouted weevils on the tender flush
Leaf-cutting weevil.spread: Adult weevils fly between trees, and the grubs develop in the cut leaf pieces on the ground before entering the soil to pupate.
Leaf-cutting weevil.action: Collect and burn the cut leaf pieces from the ground every day during flushing.

treatment.name: Daily collection and burning of fallen cut leaves
treatment.notes: The eggs and grubs are inside these pieces; this breaks the cycle.

treatment.name: Neem oil 1500 ppm
treatment.notes: On the new flush at 7-day intervals to deter feeding and egg laying.

treatment.name: Lambda-cyhalothrin 5 EC
treatment.notes: Only on new flush of nursery plants and young trees when weevils are many; not on open flowers.

Powdery mildew.name: Powdery Mildew
Powdery mildew.description: Fungal disease of panicles, young fruits and tender leaves, favoured by cool nights and cloudy weather at flowering. It causes heavy flower and fruitlet drop and can destroy most of the crop.
symptoms: White powdery growth on panicles, flowers and young fruits
Flowers and pea-size fruits turn brown and drop
White powder on the underside of young leaves
Young leaves twist and show purplish-brown patches
Powdery mildew.spread: Wind-borne spores spread from infected leaves and old panicles to the new panicles.
Powdery mildew.action: Spray wettable sulphur at panicle emergence and follow with a systemic fungicide 15 days later.

treatment.name: Wettable sulphur 80 WP
treatment.notes: First spray when panicles are 8-10 cm long; avoid in hot weather above 35 °C.

treatment.name: Hexaconazole 5 EC
treatment.notes: Second spray 15 days after the first.

treatment.name: Azoxystrobin 23 SC
treatment.notes: Alternative for the second or third spray; also checks anthracnose.

Sooty mold.name: Sooty Mould
Sooty mold.description: Black fungal growth that lives on the sticky honeydew dropped by hoppers, scales and mealybugs. It does not infect the leaf but blocks sunlight and soils the fruits.
symptoms: Black soot-like film on the upper leaf surface that rubs or peels off
Sticky, shiny honeydew on leaves
Hoppers, scales or mealybugs on shoots and panicles, often with ants
Blackened panicles and fruits in severe cases
Sooty mold.spread: The mould grows wherever sap-sucking insects deposit honeydew, and its spores are carried by wind and rain.
Sooty mold.action: Control the sap-sucking insects that produce the honeydew and wash off the black film with a starch spray.

treatment.name: Starch (maida) solution 5%
treatment.dose: 1 kg boiled in 5 L water, diluted to 20 L
treatment.notes: The dried starch flakes off and takes the black mould with it.

treatment.name: Imidacloprid 17.8 SL
treatment.notes: Against mango hoppers at panicle emergence, before flowers open.

treatment.name: Pruning of dense, overlapping branches
treatment.notes: Hoppers and mould build up in shaded, crowded canopies.

healthy.name: Healthy
healthy.description: The leaf shows no sign of disease, pest or deficiency. Keep watching the new flush and the panicles, where most problems begin.
symptoms: Uniform green leaves without spots, galls or black film
No white powder on leaves or panicles
Normal new flush
healthy.spread: Not applicable - no disease or pest detected.
healthy.action: Continue regular pruning, balanced manuring and weekly scouting, especially during flushing and flowering.
